title: Dawar Qatar: An Industrial Supply Website Built to Win More RFQs
storyLead: How Teknoppy designed dawarqatar.com so oil and gas, construction and marine buyers in Doha can find 12 product lines and request a quote, upload a BOQ or WhatsApp the team in seconds.
services: UX and UI design, website development, content structure, on-page SEO setup
atAGlance: Teknoppy designed and built dawarqatar.com, the website of Dawar Global Trading and Contracting, an industrial supplier in Doha, Qatar
The site presents 12 product lines for oil and gas, construction and marine buyers
"Request a Quote", WhatsApp and phone stay in the header, and buyers can upload a BOQ from the homepage
Ordering is explained in four simple steps
Dawar's own published figures: 12 product lines, a 24-hour quote promise, 7 industries served and 5 delivery zones
aboutParagraphs: Dawar Global Trading and Contracting supplies oilfield equipment, PPE, lifting gear, welding consumables, valves, NDT instruments and more to contractors, operators and facility teams across Qatar. Its buyers do not browse for fun. They arrive with a part number, a BOQ or an urgent shutdown list.

Dawar is a Doha-based trading and contracting company that acts as a single supplier for industrial projects. It sources products, matches them to technical specifications and delivers onshore and offshore. It works with brands such as Doppler for ultrasonic NDT, Jireh Inspection Robotics, Hanna Instruments, TB Wood's and Troncoflex, and offers procurement, project support and logistics services.

Its local team understands In-Country Value requirements, which matters to Qatar's oil and gas operators. It serves oil and gas, petrochemical, construction, marine, power and manufacturing, and delivers to Doha, the Industrial Area, Ras Laffan, Mesaieed, Dukhan and offshore supply bases. The website had to make all of this clear in seconds.
challengeLead: Three problems shaped the design brief.

challenges.title: Twelve very different product lines on one site
challenges.description: Safety shoes, chain blocks, E7018 electrodes, cable glands and phased array NDT kits have different buyers. Without a clear structure, visitors would get lost and leave for a competitor.

challenges.title: Buyers want to send an RFQ, not fill a cart
challenges.description: Industrial buyers in Qatar usually work from a BOQ or a part list. They want to send it, get a price and move on. A standard contact page buried in the footer would slow them down.

challenges.title: Proving trust in a high-risk industry
challenges.description: Oil and gas buyers need certified products. The site had to show standards like API, ASME, ATEX and IECEx, test certificates, real brands and a real Doha address before a buyer would send a PO.

objectiveLead: Design a fast, mobile-friendly industrial website that organises 12 product lines by product, industry and service, puts a quote request on every screen, and builds trust with certifications, brands and projects, so more visitors become qualified RFQs.
objectives: Organise 12 product lines by product, industry and service
Put a quote request on every screen
Build trust with certifications, brands and projects
approachLead: Five design pillars, each tied to how industrial buyers order.

approachPillars.title: Clear navigation for 12 product lines
paragraphs: We built a mega menu for Products, Industries, Services, Brands, Guides and Contact, with a separate Product Catalogue menu. The homepage shows 12 numbered category cards with images and a "Most Requested Items" strip for fast movers such as safety shoes, chain blocks and hydraulic torque wrenches.

approachPillars.title: An RFQ-first layout
paragraphs: The header keeps phone, WhatsApp and "Request a Quote" visible at all times. The hero has a quick-quote box where buyers type a part number or upload a BOQ. A four-step "How to Order" section explains RFQ, quotation, PO and delivery, and the contact form also accepts BOQ files.

approachPillars.title: Trust-first design
paragraphs: A trust bar under the hero shows one-stop supply, certified products, 24-hour quotes, test certificates and onshore and offshore delivery. Brand partners, recent projects, eight "Why Choose Dawar" points, the office address and working hours all sit on the homepage.

approachPillars.title: Industry pages that speak the buyer's language
paragraphs: Seven industry sections with photography show oil and gas, construction and marine teams that Dawar understands their sites. A delivery coverage block names Ras Laffan, Mesaieed and Dukhan, the places buyers actually work.

approachPillars.title: Mobile speed and accessibility
paragraphs: Site engineers often order from their phones. The layout is fully responsive, images carry descriptive alt text, and assets are kept light so pages load quickly on mobile data.

deliverables.description: Instant contact on desktop and mobile.

deliverables.title: 7 industry sections
deliverables.description: Buyers see their own sector reflected.

deliverables.title: 4-step How to Order
deliverables.description: Clear process from RFQ to delivery.

whyMattersHeading: Why RFQ-first design wins industrial B2B in Qatar
whyMattersParagraphs: In industrial supply, the website's job is not to sell online. It is to get the buyer's BOQ into the sales team's inbox before a competitor's. Every extra click between landing and quoting costs leads.

By putting quote tools on every screen, showing proof of certification and speaking to each industry, Dawar's site now works like a sales engineer that is online around the clock. That is what a good web design company in Qatar should deliver for B2B suppliers.

faqs.question: What should an industrial supplier website include?
faqs.answer: A clear product menu, a quote form with BOQ upload, WhatsApp and phone buttons, certifications and standards, brand partners, past projects, delivery areas and a real address. dawarqatar.com includes all of these.

faqs.question: Can a website let customers upload a BOQ or part list?
faqs.answer: Yes. Teknoppy added a quick-quote box and a contact form on dawarqatar.com that accept BOQ files, so buyers can send full requirements in one step.

faqs.question: Why add a WhatsApp button to a B2B website in Qatar?
faqs.answer: Many buyers and site engineers in Qatar prefer WhatsApp for quick questions. A visible button turns that habit into enquiries instead of lost visits.

faqs.question: Can Teknoppy build bilingual English and Arabic websites?
faqs.answer: Yes. Teknoppy builds multilingual websites and can add an Arabic version with right-to-left layout for Qatar and GCC audiences.

faqs.question: How long does a business website project take?
faqs.answer: It depends on pages, products and integrations. Teknoppy gives a written timeline and fixed quote after a free consultation.

faqs.question: Does Teknoppy design websites for businesses in Qatar?
faqs.answer: Yes. Teknoppy is a web design and SEO company based in Kochi, Kerala, building websites for clients in Qatar, the UAE and across the GCC.
